description: The video sequence (frames 1-10) shows a roundplate part on the linear feeder moving towards and over the ramp structure. The part successfully climbs the ramp, falls off the ledge onto the right side of the feeder, and is positioned to continue forward movement. This behavior matches the normal process description ('Climb the ramp unhindered -> Fall off the ledge onto the right side'). There are no visual signs of lateral pushes (pre-trap or post-track rejection) or orientation anomalies where the part appears falling off the track vertically relative to its motion direction.

The roundplate moves from the left side towards the ramp and appears to climb it in frames 1-4 as expected. However, in frame 5, the roundplate exhibits an anomalous orientation where it appears pushed vertically against the track/ramp structure, deviating from the normal smooth transition over the ramp seen in reference videos (RAG/Sub_sampled). Subsequent frames (9-10) show the roundplate on the far left track edge, suggesting a reversal of direction or a bounce back after being pushed off the track vertically (post-track rejection).
The roundplate lego part does not fall straight down after leaving the ramp but appears to slide off sideways at an angle, indicating it was pushed vertically rather than falling freely.

The video sequence shows a roundplate part moving towards the ramp on the linear track. It climbs the ramp unhindered and falls off the ledge onto the right side of the linear feeder, continuing to move forwards on the track. The motion appears consistent with normal process behavior where the object moves nigh unhindered across the trap ramp and continues its path. There are no visual indications of the part being pushed off vertically to the movement direction (pre-trap or post-trap rejection).

The video sequence shows an anomalous behavior where the roundplate part is pushed off the linear feeder before reaching the trap ramp area (pre-trap rejection). Instead of climbing the ramp as expected, the part is ejected vertically/obliquely outwards. The middle set of images demonstrates this anomaly where the part loses contact with the track significantly before entering the ramp zone, contrary to the normal process of moving towards and then falling off the ramp.

The video sequence shows the part approaching and climbing the ramp normally (frames 1-6), but in the later frames (specifically around frame 9-10), the part appears to fall sideways or is pushed off the track in a direction vertical to its movement, rather than cleanly falling forward onto the right feeder. This orientation suggests a lateral push or post-track rejection event where the part was knocked off its parallel trajectory.

The part (Lego roundplate) is observed moving along the linear feeder, successfully navigating the ramp trap structure and continuing its forward motion towards the right side without any signs of rejection or ejection. The sequence demonstrates normal linear vibration feeding behavior.

The video sequence shows a Lego roundplate part moving along the linear feeder. It approaches the central ramp (part trap), climbs over it, and successfully falls back onto the linear feeder on the right side to continue its forward movement. This behavior is consistent with the normal process description of passing across the trap without rejection. The part remains on the track throughout and does not exhibit signs of being pushed off vertically or misaligned.

The video sequence shows a linear vibration feeding process where a round plate part moves from left to right. It approaches the ramp/trap structure, passes over it without issue, and continues moving forward on the feeder. The part remains stable on the track surface, does not exhibit post-trap or pre-trap rejection behaviors (such as hanging off the edge vertically), and its orientation is consistent with normal movement. The process follows the expected normal behavior described in the context.

The video sequence shows an anomaly at Frame 7 where the part (white dot) stops or becomes jammed at the entrance of the ramp. The visual evidence (dark mark/absence of the white dot) suggests the part was pushed vertically relative to its movement direction prior to falling off the ramp, preventing it from continuing through the normal process of climbing the ramp unhindered.

The roundplate part is shown navigating the linear feeder and ramp structure. It appears to be climbing over the ramp or ledge in its intended direction without being pushed off the track vertically or tumbling off into an anomalous position. It remains contained on the surface, consistent with normal behavior where it would climb the trap/ramp unhindered.

The video sequence depicts the linear vibration feeding simulation in its expected normal mode. The roundplate part is observed approaching the ramp (trap), climbing it unhindered, falling off the ledge onto the right side of the linear feeder, and moving forwards on the feeder. There are no visual indicators of rejection, such as the part being pushed off the track vertically, pre-trap rejection, or post-track rejection. The object maintains proper alignment with the track throughout the sequence without deviation from the normal process behavior described.

The video sequence shows a part moving towards the ramp on the linear feeder without any visible deviation. The object appears to be climbing or engaging the ramp in a manner consistent with the described normal process (climb unhindered, fall off to right). There is no visual evidence of the part being pushed off the track sideways (pre-trap rejection) or falling off the boundary completely (post-track rejection).

The roundplate successfully traverses the linear feeder, climbs the ramp unhindered, and falls off onto the right side as expected. It does not exhibit any signs of being pushed off-track or getting stuck. The sequence aligns with the defined normal process behavior where the object moves from left to right without interruption.

The video begins with a normal process where the roundplate moves left to right, climbing the ramp unhindered and falling off the ledge onto the right side. However, in the final frames (9 and 10), the roundplate appears to be tumbling down vertically past the end of the track rather than simply falling sideways to continue on the feeder. This indicates it has been pushed off the linear feeder vertically to the part movement direction, consistent with post-trap rejection where the object falls from the right side of the ramp in an orientation that signifies exit from the system.

The provided video sequence shows a lego roundplate on a linear feeder track. The part appears stationary within the frame, which is consistent with the normal process behavior description where "the object seems still in space" due to the vibration frequency of the linear track. No visual indications are observed that the part has been pushed off the linear feeder (post-track or pre-trap rejection) or oriented as if falling off (trap rejection). The part remains contained within the track boundaries and on a level surface without overhanging non-overlapping pixels. While the video segment appears static compared to the dynamic motion seen in the normal reference (passing across the ramp), the 'stillness' is explicitly described as expected behavior for this vibrating system. Thus, the observed state is consistent with the anomaly definitions provided, which focus on push-offs and falling off.

The roundplate encounters an obstruction on the ramp structure, deviating from normal climbing behavior. It appears to interact with the vertical component of the trap rather than traversing it smoothly. In the final frame, there is evidence of a separate object mark on the linear feeder to the right side, suggesting the part was pushed off the track during this interaction.

The roundplate remains on the track and does not exhibit any signs of being pushed off (pre-trap or post-track rejection). It moves towards and passes the ramp structure without falling off, which is consistent with the described normal process behavior.

The input video sequence shows the roundplate climbing the ramp normally, but upon exiting onto the linear feeder (post-ramp), it does not align with the track. In the later frames (e.g., frame 6-7 of the input set), the part falls vertically off the linear feeder, which is inconsistent with the normal process where it should move forwards parallel to the track as observed in the sub-sampled normal video.

The video sequence shows a lego roundplate approaching the ramp and moving along the linear track. The observed motion is consistent with the normal process described: the part moves towards the ramp, climbs over it unhindered, and appears to transition to the right side of the feeder. This progression matches the reference images (RAG and sub_sampled normal video) where parts are seen moving from the upper track to the lower section on the right side without any signs of being pushed off or ejected vertically/sideways. No anomalous behaviors such as pre-trap rejection, post-track rejection, or trap rejection were detected.
